einzeiler: Exploring Ephesians 2:18 on experiencing God's love and the deep human need for access.
kurzfassung: Tim Keller examines Ephesians 2:18 to explain how the gospel unites diverse people through a common mystical experience of God. He discusses the universal human desire to belong to an inner circle and contrasts it with true spiritual access to the Father through Christ and the Holy Spirit. Ultimately, believers are invited to seek a genuine, experiential relationship with God rather than merely intellectual assent.
stichpunkte: Ephesians 2:18 highlights two ways God unites diverse people: through the legal position of Christ's blood and a common mystical experience.
The word both signifies that any two disparate individuals can become part of the same new humanity.
Christianity is designed to be experienced, not just understood intellectually.
Human beings possess an intense, universal drive to be on the inside of exclusive groups, as C.S. Lewis outlines.
Searching for acceptance through worldly inner rings ultimately leads to emptiness.
Spiritual access to the Father is granted exclusively through Jesus Christ as an advocate.
The Holy Spirit illuminates biblical truths and helps believers experience divine love during prayer.

kapitel.titel: The Mystical Experience of God's Love
Access to the Father and the Inner Ring
Through Christ and by the Spirit

clips.hook: Attempting to introduce yourself to someone powerful without an intermediary.
clips.text: Trying to approach a major figure directly without someone to vouch for you is impossible and impractical if everyone attempted it.

clips.hook: A loving father welcoming a child who simply wants to spend time together.
clips.text: When a child expresses a desire for more closeness and affection, a parent naturally responds with warmth rather than punishment.
